newsitem.title: BOSNIA: Croat militia expels Moslems from west Mostar.
newsitem.headline: Croat militia expels Moslems from west Mostar.

text.p: U.N. relief workers reported on Tuesday that the Bosnian Croat army was involved in a brutal campaign of expulsions against Moslems in the Croat-held sector of the divided southern city of Mostar.

A spokesman for the U.N. High Commissioner for Refguees (UNHCR) said some 18 evictions were reported in six weeks in west Mostar and members of the Croat militia (HVO) were implicated in the "ethnic cleansing".

The latest expulsion occurred on Monday when a group of men, including several in Bosnian Croat militia (HVO) uniforms, changed the lock on an apartment door while the Moslem tenant looked on, UNHCR spokesman Kris Janowski said.
The soldiers searched through cupboards and drawers for money and threatened the 56-year-old man if he reported the incident.

A UNHCR report quoted the soldiers as saying: "If you are going to be nice, you can take some of your belongings. If you intend to go and see the police, you cannot take anything and you will get hurt."

The U.S.-brokered peace treaty that ended the Bosnian war last year supposedly obliges Bosnia's factions to respect human rights of minorities, but Janowski said ethnic cleansing in Mostar was on the rise.
There had been 70 expulsions in west Mostar since the Dayton peace agreement was signed a year ago, he said.
"The (Croat) authorities are either unwilling or unable to stop it. The scale and the persistence of the evictions indicates the authorities have given a quiet nod to it," Janowski told Reuters.
"Certainly it's the most intense wave of evictions we have seen."
Mostar was devastated in heavy fighting during a 10-month Croat-Moslem war that coincided with the main conflict in Bosnia between Serbs and the Moslem-led government.
The two sides agreed to form a federation and to reunify Mostar, but the the city remains strictly divided into Croat and Moslem sectors.
The expulsions of the few Moslems remaining in west Mostar has created a housing shortage in east Mostar, UNHCR officials said.
The NATO-led peace force condemned the expulsions and said commanders were considering taking punitive measures against the Croats.
"The evictions ...are despicable and there is a body of evidence to suggest HVO involvement," Major Brett Boudreau told reporters.
The deputy commander of the NATO peace force in Bosnia was due to discuss the situation with the commissioner of the international police, he said.
"We take this extremely seriously and if the evidence holds firm there will be military consequences (for the Croats)," Boudreau said without elaborating.
